title: Vegan mushroom risotto
subtitle: Creamy risotto without butter or cheese
excerpt: A rich, creamy vegan mushroom risotto that achieves its silky texture through good stock and the starch of carnaroli rice alone. No butter, no Parmesan. Deeply flavoured from porcini and chestnut mushrooms.
sourceNotes: Vegan adaptation of the classic northern Italian mushroom risotto. The technique is the standard risotto method; the creaminess comes from the rice starch and a generous amount of good olive oil at the mantecatura stage.

content.text: The secret to a creamy vegan risotto is the mantecatura technique at the end: remove from heat and beat vigorously with a generous pour of extra-virgin olive oil. The starch released from the rice during cooking, combined with the oil, creates an emulsified, creamy texture that rivals the butter-and-cheese version. Ensure the stock is well seasoned and flavourful; weak stock makes a weak risotto.

items.prepNote: hot, kept just below a simmer; must be well seasoned
soaked in 150 ml hot water, liquid reserved
divided: 30 ml for cooking, 50 ml for mantecatura

content.text: Soak the dried porcini in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain and reserve the soaking liquid; chop the porcini roughly.
Heat 30 ml oil in a wide casserole. Fry the fresh mushrooms over high heat until golden, 5 to 6 minutes. Add the porcini and cook 1 minute more. Remove and set aside.

In the same pot, cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and thyme and cook 1 minute. Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring. Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.

Add the porcini soaking liquid (leaving the last gritty tablespoon behind) and the sautéed mushrooms. Then add stock a ladle at a time, stirring after each addition, for 18 to 20 minutes until the rice is just cooked through.

Remove from heat. Pour over the remaining 50 ml extra-virgin olive oil and beat vigorously for 1 to 2 minutes until the risotto becomes creamy and glossy. Season generously. Rest for 2 minutes. Serve in warm bowls scattered with parsley.

items.cause: Oil not beaten in vigorously enough at the end
items.fix: Beat hard off the heat. The emulsification requires real agitation. Some cooks shake the pot back and forth vigorously.

items.cause: Stirred too aggressively throughout or too much starch released
items.fix: Stir regularly rather than continuously. Some starchiness is correct; excessive glueyness means the rice was overworked.
Use the best vegetable stock you can make or buy. The porcini soaking liquid adds depth; don't skip it.

items.cause: Not enough stock or insufficient time
items.fix: Continue adding stock and cooking. Taste a grain from the 18-minute mark onward.

content.text: Risotto as a fully plant-based dish is not a modern invention. The core technique has always relied on stock, wine, and the starch of the rice for its character; the butter and Parmesan of the mantecatura are finishing enrichments that can be replaced. In northern Italy it is perfectly standard to finish a mushroom risotto with nothing but good olive oil, particularly in autumn when porcini are at their peak. The result depends on the quality of the mushrooms and the stock, not on dairy.
